attempts.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: one original-size-compatible Hearts of Iron IV character portrait replacement.
Image 1 is the original HOI4 portrait and composition target. Image 2 is the user's exact 奶龙 identity reference: a smooth golden-yellow round creature with green rings around black eyes, a small horizontal mouth and creamy belly.
Replace the human head, body and exposed human skin with this recognizable yellow mascot. RETAIN the original person's visible hairstyle, hairline, hair color, eyebrows, moustache, beard and sideburns as distinguishing features attached to the mascot, adapting them to its round head. Match the original's parting, thickness, curls and facial-hair shape. Preserve a bald scalp or clean-shaven face only where the original actually has one. Do not invent hair hidden under a hat.
Preserve the original garment design, uniform type, fabric, colors, headgear, glasses, decorations, accessories, expression, gaze, pose, action, framing, lighting, background and painterly color treatment. RETAILOR the collar/neck opening and shoulder fit to the mascot rather than copying a narrow human neck opening. Keep all existing garment design details and insignia; do not invent new hats, uniforms, medals or symbols. Use only visually present features; do not infer appearance from filenames or historical biographies.
Keep the yellow creature's anatomy, large green-ringed black eyes and small horizontal mouth; do not restore human skin, human nose or human ears. Express the original mood through its creature eyes and mouth plus retained eyebrows.
Collar and anatomy: use a compact rounded mascot head seated close to broad shoulders, with a very short, wide neck transition. No tall cylindrical/giraffe neck, no long tapered yellow stalk above the clothing. The entire neck base must fit INSIDE a correctly sized collar opening. Widen and reshape the collar opening naturally around that base while keeping the original collar style, tabs, piping and badges. Collar front sits visibly in front of the lower neck; collar back sits behind it, with coherent perspective, contact shadow and fabric tension. No neck clipping through collar, pinched narrow ring, floating collar, broken seam or abrupt geometric junction. The creamy belly stays under opaque clothing; never add a cream/white bib on the neck. Respect this fit even for tiny advisor or pilot portraits.
The head silhouette is nearly round or a SHORT egg shape. Its chin rests immediately above the garment collar, without copying the original human neck length. Preserve the shoulder position and crop by broadening the fitted garment; do not fill that space with a tall yellow column.
Keep the source's fastening state: a buttoned closed standing collar remains closed and buttoned, with both front ends meeting naturally at the center seam. Do not turn a closed military collar into a deep V-neck or unbuttoned shirt. Preserve open lapels/shirt collars only where the original is actually open.
Preserve the source aspect ratio, crop and number of figures. Preserve real alpha transparency, photographic frames, note cards and existing decorative markings where present. Do not add such framing where absent. Polished painterly HOI4 finish, legible at the original in-game size. One source image to one asset. No comparison board, new text, label, watermark or extra figure.

Visible source-specific features: Bald scalp, clean-shaven face without moustache or beard. Dark olive uniform with red/gold star collar tabs, brass buttons and original white collar edge. Preserve closed collar and stern three-quarter gaze. Retain these original visible hair/accessory details on the yellow mascot; moustache above its small horizontal mouth, specified beard below it. Head nearly round, chin close to the properly fitted garment collar, very short wide neck, coherent front/back collar occlusion and contact shadow. No invented headgear, medals, human ears or nose, long yellow neck or cream neck bib.
Output alpha: keep a genuine fully transparent RGBA background outside the portrait silhouette. No painted gray backdrop, halo, studio gradient or rectangular plate. Retain the source's clothing, hair, headgear and portrait crop.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one HOI4 mascot portrait correction for coherent neck and clothing fit.
Image 1 is the current generated yellow mascot portrait to edit. Image 2 is the original game portrait, specifying the original garment style, hair, facial hair, hat, accessories, pose, expression and fastening state. Image 3 is the user's exact mascot anatomy reference: a compact rounded golden-yellow creature with green-ringed black eyes and a small horizontal mouth.
Correct only the head-neck-collar-shoulder fit. Replace the overlong yellow cylinder or tapered neck stalk with a compact round head sitting LOW and close to broad shoulders, with almost no exposed neck. Do not squeeze a thick creature into a narrow human collar ring. Widen and retailor the original collar opening around the creature's actual neck base, so the whole base sits INSIDE it. The front collar cloth occludes the lower neck, and the rear collar sits behind it; show coherent fabric tension, contact shadow, seams and perspective. Preserve original fabric, collar style, tabs, piping, badges and existing decorations, adjusting their size/placement to the wider fitted collar. Do not add symbols, awards, accessories or a different outfit.
CRITICAL fastening rule: if Image 2 has a closed, buttoned standing military collar, it must remain fully CLOSED and buttoned. Both front ends meet at the same level at the center seam; no deep V-shaped opening, unbuttoned tunic or exposed yellow chest wedge. Widen the whole collar circumference instead of opening its front. For an originally open shirt or lapel collar, preserve that open style and tie/scarf with correctly fitted overlapping layers. A white shirt collar or scarf stays textured fabric; it is not a cream belly patch.
The mascot keeps its yellow anatomy, green-ringed black eyes and small horizontal mouth. Preserve the original visible hairstyle, hairline, color, eyebrows, moustache and beard where actually present in Image 2; preserve a clean-shaven chin where appropriate. Do not invent facial hair, human skin, nose or ears. Preserve headgear, glasses, pipe, facial mood, head turn, shoulders/body orientation, painted background or genuine transparency, and source portrait aspect ratio. Preserve photo frames and note cards exactly where present. The cream belly stays under the clothes: no white/cream neck bib, skin-colored collar gap, detached ring, pinched fabric, clipped neck, floating collar or long giraffe/sausage neck. One final portrait, no comparison layout or new text.

Targeted correction: this bald mascot head is too tall and tapers into a long yellow column above the collar. Make the head nearly ROUND, shorten the lower face markedly, and seat the chin immediately above broad shoulders with only a very short wide neck transition. Preserve bald scalp, original brows, clean-shaven face, gaze, olive tunic, red/gold star collar tabs and brass buttons. The standing collar stays CLOSED, with its front ends meeting at the center. Adjust the garment's width/shoulders to keep the original crop rather than extending the yellow head. No cream neck bib or invented facial hair.
Output alpha: keep a genuine fully transparent RGBA background outside the portrait silhouette. No painted gray backdrop, halo, studio gradient or rectangular plate. Retain the source's clothing, hair, headgear and portrait crop.
